issue: Does Rule 32.1's bar on hearsay evidence apply at the sentencing phase of a supervised-release revocation, or is that phase governed by Rule 32's general sentencing procedure, which gives the court broad discretion to accept hearsay?
provision: Fed. R. Crim. P. 32.1; Fed. R. Crim. P. 32

sides.position: Rule 32.1's protections against hearsay extend to the sentencing phase of a revocation proceeding
cases: United States v. Navarro-Santisteban, 83 F.4th 44 (1st Cir. 2023)

sides.position: The sentencing phase of a revocation proceeding is governed by Rule 32's general sentencing procedure, which gives the court broad discretion to accept hearsay
cases: United States v. Navarro-Santisteban, 83 F.4th 44 (1st Cir. 2023)

quote: See United States v. Torres-Santana, 991 F.3d 257, 265 (1st Cir. 2021) (recognizing circuit split on the issue and declining to resolve the legal question where facts made it unnecessary to do so).
cite: United States v. Navarro-Santisteban, 83 F.4th 44 (1st Cir. 2023)
